transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting stuck on this thought while I’m driving my cab. Like, even if I know I already did the safety check, my mind keeps telling me maybe I missed something and someone could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied about checking it.

I know that probably sounds a bit much, and I don’t want to waste your time, but it’s hard to make it stop, even when I’m trying to focus on driving or study afterward.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to make these thoughts go away or to feel safer?

Yeah… I mean, I do check things. Probably more than I should.

Before I take a ride, I go around the car and check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork… and then sometimes I’m not sure it “counted,” if that makes sense, so I start again. I’ve even taken pictures of things just to prove to myself I checked them.

I know it sounds kind of excessive. I don’t want to make it seem like I’m careless or anything—actually it’s the opposite—but sometimes passengers are waiting and I’m already late, and I still feel like I have to restart the whole check if it doesn’t feel right.
Do you feel anxious or on edge when you're not thinking about the safety checks or driving?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think I’m anxious all the time or anything. It’s mostly when that thought gets going, like around the car stuff.

When I’m doing other things, I guess I can feel a bit tense sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s just normal stress. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you have any other habits or rituals that you feel compelled to do over and over, outside of checking the car?

Not really outside of the car, I don’t think. I mean… the main thing is still before rides. I keep going around checking the tires, lights, doors, the meter, paperwork, all of that.

I know I already said some of this, sorry. It’s just sometimes I’ll finish and then it doesn’t feel like I really checked it properly, so I start over. I’ve taken pictures too, just to reassure myself. Even if passengers are waiting and I’m late, I still feel like I need to do it again.
Does doing these checks over and over affect your ability to do your job as a cab driver or impact other parts of your life?

Yeah… it does, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not trying, because I really am, but I’ve lost some rides because I couldn’t get on the road fast enough. And I’ve gotten warnings about being late or not being available when I’m supposed to be.

It kind of spills over too. I’ve been meaning to study for my CDL, but then so much of the day gets eaten up by rechecking and trying to catch up after, so I keep pushing it back. And I don’t really see my friends much anymore. Not because I don’t want to, just… I’m either behind on work or trying to make up for time I lost. Does that make sense?
Do these thoughts about possibly missing something in your safety checks ever occur to you when you're not driving or preparing to drive?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, it’s mostly tied to the cab, but it doesn’t just stop once I’m away from it.

Like if I’m driving, even after I know I checked everything, I’ll get this thought that maybe I missed something and somebody could get hurt, or my boss might think I lied about doing it. And it can pop up when I’m trying to study too, which is embarrassing to say, because I know I already did the check. It just keeps coming back and I can’t really make it shut up. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever have repetitive thoughts like this about things other than your job or the safety of your cab?

Not really other things, no… at least not that I can think of. It’s mostly the cab and the safety check.

Like, that’s kind of why I came in. Even when I know I did it, I’ll get hit with this thought that I missed something and someone could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied about checking. And it doesn’t just stay at the garage or whatever — it comes up while I’m driving, or when I’m trying to study, and I can’t really make it quiet.

I know that probably sounds repetitive, but that’s the main thing.
Are your repetitive thoughts mostly about preventing something bad from happening or making a mistake?

Yeah… mostly that, I think. It’s not like I’m trying to think about it, but it’s this worry that I made some mistake on the safety check, even when I know I did it.

Like, I’ll be driving or trying to study, and it just hits me that maybe I missed something on the cab and somebody could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied about checking it. I know that sounds kind of… intense, but it’s hard to make it stop. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How much distress do these thoughts about possibly missing something in your safety checks cause you?

It’s… pretty upsetting, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it gets bad enough that I can’t just brush it off.

Even when I know I did the safety check, the thought keeps hitting me that I missed something on the cab and someone could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied about doing it. And then I’m driving or trying to study and it’s still there, like I can’t make it shut up. It makes me really tense. Is that the kind of distress you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with family or friends since these thoughts and checking behaviors started?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m cutting everybody off on purpose, but I barely see my friends anymore.

A lot of the time I’m behind because I couldn’t get on the road on time, or I’m trying to catch up after the checking took too long. I’ve lost some rides and gotten warnings, so then I feel like I should be working more, not hanging out. And my studying for my CDL keeps getting pushed back too, because so much of the day gets eaten up.

So… yeah, it’s affected things. Not because I don’t care about people, just… I’m always behind. Is that what you mean?
Have you had to turn down or avoid any other opportunities or activities besides spending time with friends because of these thoughts or checking behaviors?

Yeah… I mean, not a ton of big things, I guess, but it does get in the way.

I’ve lost some rides and gotten warnings because I can’t get on the road when I’m supposed to. And I keep meaning to study for my CDL, but then the checking takes up so much of the day that I’m either behind on work or trying to catch up.

So besides friends, it’s mostly work stuff and studying. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just making excuses, but… yeah, it has made me miss out on things I should be doing.
Have you felt like you've had to give up or significantly cut back on any hobbies or activities you enjoy because of these thoughts or checking behaviors?

Yeah… I guess I have cut back, though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just blaming everything on that.

It’s mostly that I barely see friends anymore, and stuff I’d normally do after work just kind of doesn’t happen. If the checking makes me late getting on the road, then I lose rides or get warned, and then I feel like I have to make up for it. And my CDL studying keeps getting pushed back too, because so much of the day gets eaten up.

So… yeah, I’ve had to give up some of the normal stuff I enjoy, mostly because I’m always behind or trying to catch up. Is that answering it right?
Have you felt like your thoughts and checking behaviors have affected your overall quality of life?

Yeah… I think it has. I don’t want to be dramatic about it, but my days don’t really feel normal anymore.

Like, I’ve lost rides and gotten warnings because I can’t get on the road on time, and then I’m stressed trying to make up for it. My CDL studying keeps getting pushed back too, because so much of the day just gets eaten up by the checking.

And I barely see friends now, not because I don’t want to, but because I’m either behind on work or trying to catch up after I got delayed. So… yeah, I guess it’s affected my quality of life a lot. Does that make sense?
Are there any other areas of your life where you feel like these thoughts or checking behaviors are causing problems or making it hard for you to function?

Um… I think it’s mostly those same areas, honestly. Work is the biggest one, because if I can’t get on the road on time, I’ve lost rides and gotten warnings, and then I’m kind of scrambling to catch up.

And then my CDL studying keeps getting pushed back. I keep telling myself I’ll do it later, but the checking takes up so much of the day that later doesn’t really happen.

Social stuff too… I barely see friends anymore, not because I don’t want to, just because I’m either behind on work or trying to make up for being delayed. So yeah, I guess it makes functioning harder in those ways. Is that kind of what you mean?
Are there any other areas of your life, besides work and social relationships, where you feel like these thoughts or checking behaviors are causing problems?

Besides work and friends… I mean, I guess the main thing is my CDL studying. I know that’s sort of career-related too, but it’s not exactly my job right now.

I keep planning to sit down and study, and then the checking takes up so much of the day that I’m already behind or tired, and I push it off again. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not trying, because I am, but it keeps getting pushed back.

Other than that, it’s mostly the same stuff I said — losing rides, getting warnings, then trying to catch up. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by other areas.
Do you feel like these thoughts about possibly missing something in your safety checks are a part of you, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?

I don’t think it feels like it’s coming from outside of me, exactly. It feels like my own thought… just way too loud, if that makes sense.

Like, I can know I did the safety check, but then this thought hits me that maybe I missed something on the cab and somebody could get hurt, or my boss could think I lied about checking it. And I try to tell myself it’s fine, but it doesn’t really shut up, even when I’m driving or trying to study.

I know that probably sounds… I don’t know, excessive. But it feels like it’s in my head, not like someone else is putting it there. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like these thoughts about possibly missing something in your safety checks are something you want to have, or do they feel unwanted to you?

No, I don’t want them. I mean, I know safety checks are important, so I don’t want to sound like I’m trying to ignore that or be careless… but the thought itself feels really unwanted.

Like even after I know I checked the cab, it keeps coming back that I missed something and somebody could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied about doing it. I’ll be driving or trying to study and it’s still there, and I’m just trying to make it stop. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like these thoughts about possibly missing something in your safety checks are in line with your own values and beliefs?

I mean… yes and no, I guess. Safety matters to me a lot, so the part about wanting the cab to be safe is definitely in line with what I believe.

But the way the thought keeps hitting me — like even when I know I did the safety check, it says I missed something and somebody could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied — that doesn’t feel like me trying to be responsible anymore. It feels… too much, and I can’t make it shut up when I’m driving or trying to study.

I don’t want to be careless, but I also don’t want my head stuck on it like that. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like these thoughts about possibly missing something in your safety checks are consistent with the kind of person you think you are?

I guess… partly, because I do think of myself as someone who tries to be careful and not put people at risk. So in that sense, checking the cab and caring about it feels like me.

But the part where even after I know I did the safety check, the thought keeps coming back that I missed something and somebody could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied… that doesn’t feel like the kind of person I’m trying to be. It feels more like my brain won’t let it go.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I came in because I can’t really make it shut up, even when I’m driving or trying to study. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
Do you think your symptoms are significantly interfering with your overall well-being or daily life?

Yeah… I think it is, more than I probably want to admit.

I mean, I’m still trying to work and keep up, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just doing nothing, but… I’ve lost rides because I can’t get on the road on time, and I’ve gotten warnings for it. And my CDL studying keeps getting pushed back because so much of the day gets eaten up by the checking and then trying to catch up after.

I also barely see my friends anymore. It’s not like I’m trying to avoid people, I’m just always behind on work or trying to make up the time I lost. So… yeah, I guess it’s affecting my daily life a lot. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
